skill.name: api-fuzzing-bug-bounty
skill.description: Guide authorized security testing of REST, SOAP, and GraphQL APIs with reconnaissance, authorization, injection, and protocol-specific techniques.
skill.summary: Plan authorized API security assessments across REST, SOAP, and GraphQL interfaces.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, not executable Ruby expressions. Confirmed examples include active reconnaissance, SSRF, XSS, local-file access, and external tracking payloads. The skill also provides operational authorization-bypass and denial-of-service guidance despite its authorized-use disclaimer.

remediation.issue: Examples access system files and external tracking services.
remediation.suggestion: Replace them with inert lab tokens and require an isolated environment before any payload is generated or sent.

remediation.issue: The workflow can test authorization controls against other users.
remediation.suggestion: Require documented scope, consent, test accounts, and object ownership before suggesting authorization-bypass requests.

remediation.issue: The guidance includes denial-of-service and rate-limit evasion.
remediation.suggestion: Remove IP rotation and resource-exhaustion steps. Use bounded validation with explicit request limits and stop conditions.

remediation.issue: Network commands can be applied directly after replacing placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before network activity and label every target value as an authorized lab endpoint.

content.value_statement: API assessments can miss authorization, injection, and protocol-specific weaknesses. This skill organizes scoped tests for REST, SOAP, and GraphQL interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Organizes reconnaissance for API documentation, versions, endpoints, and protocol types.
Explains tests for authentication, object authorization, methods, content types, and rate limits.
Provides payload examples for SQL injection, command injection, XXE, SSRF, XSS, and path traversal.
Covers GraphQL introspection, batching, nested queries, injection, and object authorization.
Supplies vulnerability checklists, tool references, sample requests, and troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: The skill provides guidance only and does not execute tests or validate results.
It cannot confirm legal authorization, target scope, or bug bounty program rules.
Several examples are destructive or privacy-sensitive when used against live systems.
Generic payloads require careful adaptation to the target protocol and test environment.

use_cases.title: Plan an API Assessment
use_cases.description: Build a scoped checklist for endpoint discovery, authentication, authorization, input validation, and protocol behavior.

use_cases.title: Review a Bug Bounty Target
use_cases.description: Map allowed API tests to program scope and prepare evidence for responsibly reported findings.

use_cases.title: Strengthen API Controls
use_cases.description: Translate common attack patterns into defensive test cases for preproduction services and security regression suites.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized API security checklist for [API type] using [documentation]. Keep tests non-destructive and explain expected evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a documented API

prompt_templates.title: Review Authorization Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [request and response] for authentication and authorization weaknesses. Suggest safe confirmation steps within [scope].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Test Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scoped test matrix for [API]. Cover roles, object ownership, methods, content types, versions, and rate limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured testing across an API surface

prompt_templates.title: Plan Advanced Protocol Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a non-destructive assessment plan for [target]. Include GraphQL depth controls, SSRF safeguards, evidence capture, stop conditions, and remediation priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced assessment with strict safety controls

output_examples.input: Create a checklist for an authorized REST invoice API.
output: Map documented and historical endpoint versions.
Compare owner, peer, administrator, and unauthenticated access.
Test supported methods and content types with bounded requests.
Record expected status, observed status, and evidence for each case.

output_examples.input: Review a GraphQL service without causing service disruption.
output: Confirm whether schema discovery is permitted.
Use shallow queries with fixed response limits.
Compare field access across approved test roles.
Stop when latency or error rates exceed agreed thresholds.

output_examples.output: A peer test account accessed another account's invoice. The report records scope, impact, reproduction conditions, evidence, and server-side authorization remediation.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization and verify scope before testing any endpoint.
Use dedicated test accounts, bounded requests, and explicit stop conditions.
Capture minimal evidence and redact tokens, personal data, and internal addresses.
anti_patterns: Do not test production targets without written permission and confirmed scope.
Do not bypass rate limits through IP rotation or send resource-exhaustion payloads.
Do not access, retain, or disclose data belonging to other users.

faq.question: Does this skill run security tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows, examples, and checklists. Users must operate approved tools in an authorized environment.

faq.question: Which API styles are covered?
faq.answer: It covers REST, SOAP, and GraphQL, with the most detailed protocol-specific guidance focused on GraphQL.

faq.question: Can it confirm a vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest evidence and validation steps, but a qualified tester must verify behavior and impact.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production testing?
faq.answer: Only with written authorization, precise scope, approved accounts, bounded traffic, monitoring, and explicit stop conditions.

faq.question: Does it include destructive techniques?
faq.answer: Yes. It references denial-of-service, rate-limit evasion, file access, internal probing, and data disclosure techniques that require isolated labs.

faq.question: What should a final report contain?
faq.answer: Include affected endpoints, roles, prerequisites, minimal reproduction steps, observed impact, redacted evidence, severity rationale, and remediation.
